sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year, from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F145][F1][F8].
Net income grew only 0.4% a year over the same span, from $6.64 billion to $6.84 billion [F147][F25][F32].
Operating margin moved in steps rather than trending, from 15.5% in FY2021 to 41.3% in FY2023 [F20][F22].
Revenue rose 7.8% in FY2023 [D166], driven by $1,117 million of higher storm cost recovery revenue [P45][D166].
FPL's other revenue line grew 7.7% in FY2025 and supplied 5.5pp of the 9.8% total revenue growth [D272][D273][D236].
The filing attributes that growth to $1,091 million of storm cost recovery and $217 million of storm protection plan revenue [P18][D272].
Operating income grew 10.7%, ahead of revenue's 9.8%, for a 34.8% incremental margin [D237][D236][D256].
Diluted EPS fell 2.1% against a 1.6% net income decline, with diluted shares up 0.6% [D240][D238][D251].
The filing ties NEER's higher results, to $2.98 billion of net income [S29], to new investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Operating margin of 32.1% sits above its 30.3% window median [F24][D300], within a 15.5% to 41.3% range [D298][D299].
The largest move, +23.5pp in FY2023 [D177], came as revenue grew 7.8% [D166] and operating costs grew 5.1% [D179].
Operating expenses rose $566 million that year, mainly O&M and depreciation tied to NEER's growth [P42][D179].
The FY2021 drop of 14.6pp [D107] cannot be bridged from the pack, because its operating income and cost lines do not reconcile [F12][X20].
The filing ties the negative FY2025 effective tax rate of -17.7% [D226] to clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million [P11][D226].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][F32][D227], below 2.16x in FY2019 [D17] and 2.73x in FY2020 [D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241]; the filing sizes a fuel-related clause swing at $89 million, a small part of the $775 million drop [P19][F63][F64].
The pack has no capex line, so free cash flow is not shown; investing outflows were $23.9 billion, or 92.5% of revenue [F72][F8].
Net debt is $92.2 billion, or 357.4% of revenue, against $2.81 billion of cash [D231][D232][F96].
On net cash to revenue, it ranks at the 0th percentile of the four-company utilities group, against a peer median of -228.4% [D314][D315].
Dividends rose to $4.68 billion [X82], while debt issuance of $23.4 billion [X90] outpaced repayment of $10.3 billion [X98].
Return on equity of 13.1% [D235] sits above the utilities median of 11.6% [D317].
R1 flags FY2025 alone, but the current ratio was below 1.0x in every year of the window [R1][F121][F128].
The filings provided do not explain it; current liabilities of $22.8 billion exceeded current assets of $13.6 billion [F112][F104].
The longest-running flag is net debt, which has deepened for seven years [R2][D231].
Net income fell 1.6% [D238] mainly because Corporate and Other fell $1,256 million, including about $1,002 million of after-tax hedge losses [P8][P24].
The FY2024 revenue fall of 5.2% [D201][R3] reflected lower storm and fuel recovery revenue [P34], and FY2025's 9.8% growth [D236] recovered it.
Net debt above the FY2025 level of $92.2 billion [D231] in the FY2026 10-K would extend the trend; a reduction would reverse it.
Operating margin below its 30.3% window median [D300] in the FY2026 10-K would show FY2025's 32.1% [F24] not holding.
Operating cash flow below 1.83x net income [D227] in the FY2026 10-K would signal weaker cash conversion.
